title: Squares of even numbers
description: Write a function `even_squares(numbers)` that returns a list containing the square of each even number in `numbers`, using a single list comprehension. Odd numbers are skipped entirely.
hints: You need to both filter out odd numbers and transform the ones that remain into their square.
A list comprehension can combine a transformation with an `if` condition in one expression: `[expr for x in iterable if condition]`.
Use `n % 2 == 0` as the filter condition and `n * n` as the transformation: `[n * n for n in numbers if n % 2 == 0]`.
expected_behavior: Returns a list of the squares of every even element in `numbers`, preserving their original order and skipping odd elements.
solution:
def even_squares(numbers):
    return [n * n for n in numbers if n % 2 == 0]
explanation: The list comprehension iterates over `numbers`, keeps only the elements that satisfy `n % 2 == 0` (even numbers), and maps each surviving element to `n * n`, producing the list of squares in a single pass.
